unresolved_should_improve.claim: The source states that neither the magnet nor his helplessness troubled him, because he was used to that from childhood. What troubled him was the new evidence of complexity. The revision opens p12 directly with 'The magnet in its new relation', right after p11 ends on helplessness. That fuses the two troubles.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'growing complexity... contradiction' still names the real trouble, and the Adam/God/Satan figure survives.

evidence.quote: it was not the magnet or the rays or the microbes that troubled him, or even his helplessness before the forces. To that he was used from childhood.
It was not the magnet or the rays that troubled him, or even his helplessness before the forces.
it revealed a condition of human ignorance and helplessness before the commonest forces, such as his mind refused to credit.
The magnet in its new relation staggered his new education by its evidence of growing complexity, and multiplicity, and even contradiction, in life.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's sentence: 'It was not the magnet or the rays that troubled him, or even his helplessness before the forces.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (essential: 'What troubles him is growing complexity and contradiction everywhere')
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The essential claim depends on that distinction: what troubles him is growing complexity, not ignorance. Without the negation, 'new relation' and 'new education' lose their contrast.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Turn from helplessness to complexity removed in p12

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft had already cut the source's explanation that nineteenth-century diplomacy was instantly forgotten. It still kept the world's stunned silence and the 'tumultuous applause'. The revision cuts that too, so the verdict follows directly on the world being 'as astonished as himself'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Nothing so meteoric had ever been done in American diplomacy' partially sets up the verdict.

evidence.quote: after the first shock of silence, society felt the force of the stroke through its fineness, and burst into almost tumultuous applause.
society felt the force of the stroke through its fineness, and burst into almost tumultuous applause. History broke in halves.
he found most of the world as astonished as himself. History broke in halves.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Reinsert the clause 'society felt the force of the stroke through its fineness, and burst into almost tumultuous applause' before V2.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The terse verdict loses its ground: the world's submission and acclaim are what make Hay's stroke a historical break rather than a surprise. The comic sting of civilization submitting 'by mere instinct of docility' also disappears.
unresolved_should_improve.title: 'History broke in halves' now follows mere astonishment

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The source and the first draft concede that the historian's long triangulation looks 'idiotic' to the practical man, who is 'probably... in the right to-day'. The revision begins flatly 'The historian has no choice but to go on alone.'
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: p8 still contrasts the practical man with the historian.

evidence.quote: To the practical man, such an attempt is idiotic, and probably the practical man is in the right to-day; but, whichever is right
To the practical man, such an attempt is idiotic, and probably the practical man is in the right to-day; but the historian has no choice but to go on alone.
The historian has no choice but to go on alone. His walk soon becomes solitary,

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's opening clause of p9.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: Adams's characteristic self-undercutting becomes an unqualified assertion. The 'but' that motivates the solitary walk is also lost.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Concession to the practical man dropped

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts 'although Secretary of State J. Q. Adams thought himself very hardly treated' and the reference to 'the Department'. Those were the chapter's only markers that Hay holds the same office. p7 then says 'All his predecessors had suffered alike'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Hay's office may be established in an included earlier chapter (026, not supplied), and 'offer the Senate a treaty' implies it.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the clause 'although Secretary of State J. Q. Adams thought himself very hardly treated.'
